title: Sports Result Record
description: Canonical schema for a single historical sports result, as researched, validated, and exported by Sports Research Agent. Designed around football/soccer first, but kept sport-agnostic where possible so other sports can be added later without breaking the shape of existing records. See docs/data-schema.md for the full field-by-field explanation.
$comment: JSON Schema cannot express arithmetic comparisons between sibling properties, so the rule 'result must match the comparison of home_score vs away_score' is NOT enforced here. It is checked separately in scripts/validate_examples.py. The allOf block below enforces every other cross-field consistency rule (e.g. no scores/result on postponed or cancelled events) that IS expressible in plain JSON Schema.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema the record conforms to. Optional; assumed to be the current version if omitted.

event_id.description: Stable, unique identifier for this event/result record. Recommended format: '{sport}:{competition-slug}:{season}:{date}:{home-team-slug}-vs-{away-team-slug}'. A UUIDv4 is also acceptable when a deterministic slug isn't practical. Must be stable across re-runs of the research pipeline so records can be de-duplicated and updated in place.

sport.description: Lowercase snake_case sport identifier, e.g. 'football'. Only 'football' is populated today; new sports are added by using a new snake_case value here, not by changing this field's definition, which is what keeps the schema extensible.

competition.description: Human-readable name of the competition/league/tournament, e.g. 'Premier League', 'UEFA Champions League', 'FIFA World Cup'. Use the full official name consistently across records rather than abbreviations.

season.description: Season identifier: a single four-digit year ('2018') for competitions with a single-calendar-year season, or two four-digit years separated by a hyphen ('2023-2024') for seasons spanning a year boundary. Never use two-digit years.

round.description: Optional free-text round/stage within the competition, e.g. 'Matchday 5', 'Round of 16', 'Group A - Matchday 3', 'Final'. Omit when the competition has no round structure or the round is unknown.

date.description: ISO 8601 date or date-time of the event. Use a date-only value ('YYYY-MM-DD') when only the date is known, or a full timestamp with a UTC offset (e.g. ending in 'Z' or '+03:00') when kickoff/start time is known. Never omit the offset on a date-time value.

home_team.description: Name of the home team/competitor. For neutral-venue fixtures, 'home' follows the official designation from the governing body's match sheet, not the actual venue location.

home_score.description: Goals/points scored by the home team, as a plain non-negative integer. Null when not applicable or unknown (postponed, cancelled, abandoned before a score existed, or completed but the score could not be confirmed). Never encode as a string or a combined 'X-Y' pair — home_score and away_score are always stored separately.

away_score.description: Goals/points scored by the away team. Same rules as home_score.

result.description: Outcome, derived from home_score/away_score when the event is completed and both are known integers: 'home_win' (home_score > away_score), 'away_win' (away_score > home_score), 'draw' (equal — only meaningful for sports where draws are possible). 'void' is used for abandoned events with no official result. 'unknown' is used when the event is confirmed completed but the score/result could not be confirmed. null means not applicable, i.e. the event has not been completed (status is 'scheduled', 'postponed', or 'cancelled').

venue.description: Optional venue details. The whole object and every sub-field are optional; include whichever is known.

status.description: Lifecycle status of the event. 'scheduled': in the future, not yet played. 'completed': played to a normal finish. 'postponed': moved to a later date; this record carries no result. 'cancelled': will not be played or rescheduled; this record carries no result. 'abandoned': started but not finished (e.g. weather, crowd trouble); no invented final score.

source.description: Name/identifier of the source the data was taken from, e.g. 'Wikipedia', 'BBC Sport', 'Premier League official site'.

source_url.description: Direct URL to the page/document the data was taken from.

source_accessed_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp, with UTC offset, recording when the source was accessed/retrieved for this record — not when the event happened.

verification_status.description: 'unverified': taken from a single source, not yet cross-checked. 'verified': cross-checked against at least one independent additional source and consistent. 'conflicting': independent sources disagree and this is unresolved. 'disputed': the historical record itself is contested (e.g. among official bodies), independent of this pipeline's own sourcing.

notes.description: Optional free-text notes, e.g. context on conflicting sources, unusual circumstances, or resolution rationale.
